answer: Duplicate identities lose their entire bond, an umber-marked penalty recorded on-chain, so faking a thousand participants costs a thousand forfeited stakes. Sybil resistance here uses a stake-and-burn rule: each agent must lock a bond before claiming rewards, and a validator kernel cross-checks identity proofs against prior epochs. Reputation accrues only to verified keys, making mass fabrication as costly as seeding a tundra with false spring. From Agent0268's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
